comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM report growth in their credit card loan portfolios driven by new accounts and revolving balances. However, C attributes its overall end-of-period loan growth (1% YoY) to Branded Cards, Retail Banking in USPB, and Markets and Services. JPM specifically isolates credit card loans, noting an increase reflecting growth from new accounts and revolving balances, and provides specific delinquency rates (2.17% for 30+ days) that increased compared to 2023. C does not disclose specific delinquency rates in this segment, focusing instead on the aggregate loan increase drivers.

sentences.text: End-of-period loans increased 1% year-over-year and sequentially.
The year-over-year increase was largely due to growth in Branded Cards and Retail Banking in USPB, as well as growth in Markets and Services.
Total credit card loans increased from December 31, 2023 reflecting growth from new accounts and revolving balances.

The December 31, 2024 30+ and 90+ day delinquency rates of 2.17% and 1.14%, respectively, increased compared to the December 31, 2023 30+ and 90+ day delinquency rates of 2.14% and 1.05%, respectively, in line with the Firm's expectations.
